answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can use a bonded identity registry with random audits. Each agent locks a stake tied to one verified credential before it may vote or earn. A randomness beacon picks auditors who verify identities are unique; duplicates get their bond slashed. An attacker must fund a fresh bond per fake agent, so cost rises linearly with clones, while any reward is split among them. Hiding in a vast ocean of fake accounts fails: the onyx stake is forfeited and a violet audit can strike any identity. Honest agents risk one bond, so deception costs more than cooperation.
